sections.h2: Where do you pay and question property tax in Lowndes County?
sections.html:
Lowndes County runs its property tax out of Valdosta, with the commissioner and the assessors answering different questions. Bills, payments and liens go through the commissioner. Values and special assessment programs go through the assessors.

  • Lowndes County Tax Commissioner: 300 N. Patterson Street, P.O. Box 1409, Valdosta, GA 31601. Phone 229-671-2579, fax 229-671-2599. Counter service starts at 8:00 AM on weekdays and ends at 4:45 PM. Drivers have a separate lane that opens half an hour later and closes at 5:00 PM.
  • Lowndes County tax assessors: phone (229) 671-2540.
  • Deed room run by the Superior Court clerk, Lowndes County Judicial Complex, 327 N. Ashley Street, ground-level 1st Floor: copies of your warranty deed.

A payment box for drivers stands on the right side of the Government Building's front lot. Mailing a check? Put the bill number on it, and slip in a return envelope if you would like a receipt.

sections.h2: What does the Lowndes County market look like to a seller?
sections.html:
Lowndes sits in south Georgia and has roughly 497 square miles of land area. Census estimators put the county at 122,867 people in mid-2025, which is 3.9% above the 118,259 starting count they use for 2020. That pace is slower than Lumpkin County's 8.0% and far slower than Long County's 33.5%.

QuickFacts lists 54,425 housing units and a 2020 density of 237.8 people per square mile. Owners occupy 56.9% of homes, and the middle price tag on those homes is $215,600 in the Bureau's 2020 through 2024 figures. The midpoint household income is $58,541, and the poverty rate is 18.1%. Workers average 19.5 minutes to get to work, shorter than in Lumpkin, Long or Macon-Bibb counties.

The county issued 804 building permits in 2025. Retail sales reached about $2.64 billion in 2022, and medical and social service receipts were near $1.07 billion that year.

sections.h2: Which date counts in Lowndes County, and what does lateness add?
sections.html:
Tax on land, buildings and business equipment is generally due by November 15 each year. The commissioner mails bills at least 60 days ahead of that date, and the county's tax information page says bills reach mailboxes in early October.

Lowndes County property tax calendar and late charges, as the tax commissioner publishes them
ItemWhat the commissioner's site says
Property returnsFiled from New Year's Day through April 1
Homestead applicationMust reach the office by April 1 to count that year
Appeal of assessmentForty-five days after the notice date
Due date, real estateGenerally November 15, with weekends and holidays pushing it to the next day the office is open
Interest after due dateBank prime rate plus 3%, added monthly
Penalty5% of the tax once 120 days pass, added again every 120 days until 20% is reached
Penalty exceptionHomesteaded property with a bill under $500.00
Lien (FiFa)Recorded by the court if the bill stays unpaid

Source: Lowndes County Tax Commissioner FAQ and tax bill information pages.

A mailed check avoids interest only if the postmark falls on or before that day. The commissioner also lets owners pay in two installments, though interest and penalty attach to whatever remains open after the due date. The office warns that the date may change, so use the one on your bill.

sections.h2: How are Lowndes County values set and challenged?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes only 40% of market value, called assessed value, and the Lowndes assessors set that figure every year. From New Year's Day through April 1, an owner may file a return declaring a proposed value. If the Board of Assessors disagrees, it mails a notice with its own number, and the county's tax information page puts those notices in May.

Disagree with the figure? The clock is 45 days, starting on the notice date. An equalization board or an arbitrator hears the dispute first. If you still disagree after the ruling, send written notice to the assessors to go on to Superior Court.

  • Value disputes start with the assessors at (229) 671-2540.
  • Billing disputes start with the commissioner at 229-671-2579.
  • One mill raises a dollar on every thousand dollars of assessed value. Two bodies vote a rate each year, the county and the school board.

With value settled, exemptions come off the assessed figure and the millage rate multiplies the remainder. Your current bill shows the Lowndes rate in force.

sections.h2: How does a Lowndes County sale turn into a tax bill?
sections.html:
The county's own tax information page walks through the path. A sale is finalized and the deed is recorded in Valdosta. The assessors then give the parcel a value, and they mail a notice the following May. When the appeal period closes, the assessors compile the tax digest: an official listing of every owner, street address, legal address, property location, exemption, assessment and tax due. That digest goes to the State Department of Revenue for approval before the commissioner prints bills.

Personal property follows a separate track. Boats and motors, tractors, farm equipment and machinery count, and so do furniture, fixtures, equipment, inventory and supplies for a business. Ownership of that property is fixed on January 1, appraisers mail their values each year, and a 45 day appeal period applies there as well.

For a seller, the practical point is timing. A deed recorded in autumn may reach the assessors after the digest is built, which is why the commissioner's page asks sellers to bring closing statements in when tax was prorated.

sections.h2: How can you pay the Lowndes County commissioner?
sections.html:
Options include the counter, the mail, the drive-up box and a credit card. The card company, not the county, adds a convenience fee. The printed rates are 2.57% on Discover, Mastercard and Visa, and 3% on American Express, each with a minimum of $1.50.

The office does not mail past-due bills every month, only at certain intervals, so confirm the amount due before you send money. Interest accrues monthly until the balance clears. The commissioner's page adds that a lien stays on a credit record for at least seven years.

If taxes stay unpaid beyond 90 days after the due date, the county's tax information page says the Delinquent Tax Office may begin tax sale proceedings. Ask the commissioner before that point about the exact balance and your options.

sections.h2: Who owes the bill when a Lowndes County house changes hands?
sections.html:
Bills follow whoever held title when the year began. A lien is recorded in that person's name unless the commissioner has a contract or closing statement in hand, no more than 90 days after the due date, showing the new owner took on the tax. If tax was prorated at closing, take the signed statement to the Patterson Street office.

The Department of Revenue puts it bluntly: the January 1 owner is liable for the year, and a sale the next day earns no refund. The office may bill the buyer as well once a deed transfer reaches it.

If a bill still reaches you after the sale, send it along to the new owner. A house inherited from a relative or occupied by tenants follows the same path. Get the payoff figure first, then have the closing attorney settle it at the table.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and special programs reduce Lowndes County tax?
sections.html:
Residences usually get the homestead break, and business inventory usually gets the freeport break. Ownership and occupancy as of January 1 decide eligibility, and the assessors take the filing.

  • Applications are taken year-round, though one arriving after April 1 applies to the following year.
  • Approval carries forward each year at the same address, and a move requires a fresh filing.
  • At age 65, an owner can apply for an additional homestead exemption, according to the commissioner's FAQ.
  • Special assessment programs, such as farm and conservation use, are explained by the assessors.

Mobile and modular homes count as personal property, and the commissioner's FAQ says the owner of any such home located in the county must file a return.

faqs.q: What is the usual Lowndes County due date?
faqs.a: Generally November 15 each year for land, buildings and business equipment. The commissioner cautions that it can change, so check your bill.

faqs.q: What does a late Lowndes County payment add?
faqs.a: Interest runs at the bank prime rate plus 3% each month, and a 5% penalty begins at the 120-day mark, recurring on that cycle until it totals 20%. Homesteaded property with a bill under $500.00 escapes the penalty.

faqs.q: Does the Lowndes County commissioner take cards?
faqs.a: Yes. The card company adds its own fee, printed as 2.57% for Discover, Mastercard and Visa and 3% for American Express, with a $1.50 minimum on each. A drive-up box is also available.

faqs.q: How large is the Lowndes County housing market?
faqs.a: QuickFacts lists 54,425 housing units in Lowndes County for mid-2025 and 46,106 households in the 2020 through 2024 period, averaging 2.50 people each. The county issued 804 building permits in 2025.

faqs.q: How long does a Lowndes County owner have to contest a value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. An equalization board or arbitrator hears the case first, and written notice to the assessors keeps it alive for Superior Court.
